sections.h2: What are the ways to sell in St. Peters, MO?
sections.html:
St. Peters sellers can hire an agent, run the sale themselves, or take an investor's as-is cash price. Because most homes here are owner-occupied, a conventional listing has plenty of potential buyers, and a cash deal fits houses needing work or owners up against a deadline.

Survey data for 2020 to 2024 puts owner occupancy at 79.0%, the top rate among the four cities in this series.

  • Agent listing: exposure to financed buyers, plus showings and repair requests after their inspection.
  • Selling alone: no commission, but the contract and disclosures are yours to manage.
  • Investor purchase: a shorter timeline with no repair haggling, and an offer built on the buyer's estimate of the work.

sections.h2: Where did St. Peters come from, and what is it today?
sections.html:
St. Peters grew from farmland into a suburb within a single generation. Wikipedia reports that the city had only 486 people in 1970, about 15,700 by 1980 and 40,660 by 1990. It became a town in 1910 and a city in 1959. The name comes from a Jesuit mission, and a Spanish census from 1791 records an early land grant in the area. When Interstate 70 was built in 1954, crews uncovered the remains of a Mississippian village, which is why a street near the site is called Mound Drive.

Today the city covers 22.37 square miles, all land, northwest of St. Louis on the Interstate 70 corridor. It has the largest shopping center in St. Charles County, Mid Rivers Mall, and the Census Bureau reports 2022 retail sales of $86,224 per resident, far above the other three cities in this group. The population estimate for mid-2025 is 61,479, up 6.5% from the 2020 base.

Amenities that sellers can point to include a park and trail system of more than 1,000 acres, the 236,000 square foot Rec-Plex beside City Hall, and Barnes-Jewish St. Peters Hospital with 175 rooms.

The Rec-Plex hosted the 2004 Olympic Diving Trials and had an $18.5 million expansion in 2007. City government consists of a mayor and eight aldermen, two from each of four wards, and the Mayor and Board of Aldermen appoint the City Collector, City Clerk and City Treasurer. Elections are held in April.

sections.h2: Does St. Peters require an inspection when a home is sold?
sections.html:
No, as long as the home is owner-occupied. The city's Certificate of Occupancy page states plainly that St. Peters does not require an occupancy inspection for the sale of a home that is owner occupied.

The requirement bites for rentals. The city requires a Certificate of Occupancy on any change in use, tenancy or occupancy of a non-owner-occupied single-family house or a multi-family dwelling. A re-occupancy inspection is needed each time the occupant is not the owner on file with the St. Charles County Recorder of Deeds. That covers houses, townhouses, condos, duplexes and apartments, and the inspection can reach all areas of the building.

  • Owner-occupied sale: no city occupancy inspection.
  • Rented house changing tenants: application, fee, inspection and permit.
  • Applications and payments run through the city's CitizenServe portal, with questions at 636-477-6600, extension 1670.

When a tenant is living in the house you plan to sell, ask the city whether the buyer will need a fresh occupancy permit after closing.

sections.h2: Which school districts cover St. Peters addresses?
sections.html:
Three districts touch the city. The north and northwest parts are in the Fort Zumwalt School District, the southern part is in the Francis Howell School District, and a northeast sliver is in the St. Charles R-VI School District.

Three public high schools sit inside the city limits: Fort Zumwalt South, Fort Zumwalt East and Francis Howell North. Elementary schools named in the city include Fairmount, Hawthorn, Lewis and Clark, Mid Rivers, Progress South, St. Peters and Warren, with DuBray and Fort Zumwalt South Middle School also inside the boundaries. Lutheran High School of St Charles County is a private option within the city. Some St. Peters students attend schools in neighboring Cottleville or O'Fallon, so confirm the assigned school for your exact address with the district.

sections.h2: Where are St. Peters deeds recorded?
sections.html:
St. Peters lies in St. Charles County, and the county Recorder of Deeds handles its deeds from 201 N. Second Street in St. Charles, phone 636-949-7900. Per-page charges are set in the county fee schedule, which the recorder updates, so confirm the amount before you send anything in.

If you are the one recording, such as a lien release from a lender, call the office first so the document meets the format rules.

City Hall is at One St. Peters Centre Boulevard, and its main line is 636-477-6600.

sections.h2: What does water mean for a St. Peters house?
sections.html:
Heavy rain is the weather event to plan around. The National Weather Service reported 12.3 inches of rain in St. Peters on July 26, 2022, which Wikipedia describes as an unofficial record. Buyers who saw that flooding may ask about the basement, sump pump and grading, so keep records of any waterproofing or drainage work you have done.

Wikipedia's climate table for St. Peters lists a January mean minimum of 3.2 degrees Fahrenheit and a July mean maximum of 96.1 degrees. A cash buyer will price in the condition of the roof, gutters and cooling system, while a financed buyer may ask for repairs after inspection.

sections.h2: What can a St. Peters seller do to prepare the house?
sections.html:
Start by deciding who lives in the house at closing, since that determines whether the city's occupancy rules come into play at all.

  • Owner-occupied: no city occupancy inspection for the sale, so focus on repairs buyers will see.
  • Rented: ask the city about the Certificate of Occupancy that applies when the occupant changes.
  • Gather records for any basement waterproofing, sump pump or drainage work, given the July 2022 rainfall.
  • Check the school district for the address, because three districts serve the city.
  • Ask the closing agent to confirm recording costs with the county recorder.

The park and trail system, with its fishing ponds, athletic fields and picnic shelters, is a selling point that holds across districts. So is the Recycle City recycling facility, which opened in April 1997. Mention both in a listing if your house is nearby.

faqs.q: Does selling an owner-occupied house in St. Peters trigger an occupancy inspection?
faqs.a: No, not for an owner-occupied home. The city says it does not require an occupancy inspection for a sale as long as the property is owner occupied. Rentals changing tenants do need a Certificate of Occupancy.

faqs.q: What school district is St. Peters in?
faqs.a: Several. Fort Zumwalt covers the north and northwest, Francis Howell covers the south, and a northeast sliver belongs to St. Charles R-VI. Confirm the district for your address.

faqs.q: Who records a deed for a St. Peters house?
faqs.a: The St. Charles County Recorder of Deeds at 201 N. Second Street in St. Charles, reachable at 636-949-7900. The closing agent normally files it, and the fee is paid from settlement funds.

faqs.q: How high are St. Peters home values?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau lists a median of $269,900 for owner-occupied homes in its 2020 to 2024 survey, and median gross rent of $1,321.

faqs.q: Can a St. Peters rental house be sold with a tenant inside?
faqs.a: Yes, but a new occupant of a non-owner-occupied house triggers the city's occupancy permit rules. Ask the city at 636-477-6600, extension 1670, what the buyer will need after closing.
